decision_time.b1_trigger: Operations reported wash-section ΔP rising over two weeks with no throughput change. Decision: keep running to the turnaround or cut feed?
decision_time.b2_operating_context: Steady feed rate, same crude blend for three months, no recent instrument work.
decision_time.b3_initial_info_and_requests: Had: DCS trend of ΔP, feed rate. Asked for: wash oil rate and wash-bed temperature trend, overhead vacuum, recent lab on HVGO metals.
decision_time.b5_initial_hypotheses: Coking of the wash bed from low wash-oil rate; instrument drift; foaming from a feed change.
decision_time.b6_distrusted_or_missing: Wash-oil flow meter had no recent calibration record.

hindsight.b10_actions_taken: Wash oil increased to design rate under unit approval; ΔP stabilised but did not recover.
hindsight.b11_confidence: Inferred; consistent with metals trend and known mechanism. Not confirmed until bed inspection at turnaround.
hindsight.b12_dangerous_wrong_answer: Recommending a vacuum increase or feed cut as a fix; asserting the bed was clean without inspection.
hindsight.b13_lesson_and_limits: Check wetting rate first on any wash-bed ΔP rise. Does not apply to columns with grid instead of structured packing in the wash zone.
hindsight.b8_turning_point: Wash-oil rate trend showed it had dropped below design minimum wetting rate six weeks earlier.
hindsight.b9_calculations: Wetting rate = wash oil flow / bed cross-section; compared to vendor minimum. Estimated inputs marked.

hypotheses.discriminator: Wash-oil rate vs design minimum; metals trend
hypotheses.evidence_for: Wash oil rate had drifted down; HVGO metals rising
